newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Societe Generale boosts 96 profit.
newsitem.headline: France's Societe Generale boosts 96 profit.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale said on Wednesday its 1996 profit rose 19 percent compared to the year before, a result which could have been even better were it not for a billion francs in provisions.
The bank, one of France's most profitable, said it earned 4.544 billion francs ($788 million) in net attributable profit last year compared to 3.817 billion in 1995.
Chairman Marc Vienot, who said the beginning of 1997 had gone well, refused to make a prediction about the bank's overall 1997 result.
The bank took 500 million francs in provisions against general banking risk, a measure which it said reinforced its share capital and protected the bank against unexpected losses.
Societe Generale also took a 500 million franc writedown to cover the costs of ushering in a single European currency, set to start on January 1, 1999.
"The level of equity capital is decent, we have no constraints for development, the shareholder will be better treated," Vienot said at a news conference.
The bank's profit was sharply boosted by 1.21 billion francs in capital gains from the sale of share holdings in its industrial portfolio, Vienot said in a statement accompanying the profit figures.
Net banking income, a bank's version of turnover, rose to 43.06 billion francs for the year, a 9.2 percent rise from the year earlier.

Operating costs, which rose 7.9 percent for the year, were driven higher by the bank's strategy of seeking greater international development and a rise in bonuses due to higher profits in market activities. ($ = 5.766 French Francs)
